title: Voice Defense Rubric (Clinical Informatics)
description: For AI voice-session capstones where the candidate defends a CDS design, change-management plan, or implementation choice against a skeptical interlocutor playing the role of a CMIO, CMO, or skeptical attending.

levels.descriptor: Abandons the design at the first push-back, or repeats it more loudly without new content.
Defends the design but only by retreating to vaguer versions of it.
Defends the design by adding evidence and refining what is and is not being asserted.
Defends the design, narrows it where the skeptic was right to push, and the narrowed version is sharper than the original.
Never concedes, even when the skeptic is plainly correct.
Concedes only when cornered, and grudgingly.
Concedes a specific point and explains what about the design now changes.
Concedes a specific point, explains what changes, AND identifies what about the original analysis would have caught the error earlier.

criteria.name: Uses the vocabulary of the module correctly

levels.descriptor: Avoids the module's key terms (CDS Five Rights, Sittig-Singh dimensions, SAFER, etc.) or uses them wrong.
Uses the terms but as labels, not as load-bearing pieces of the argument.
Uses the terms correctly and they are doing real work in the argument.
Uses the terms correctly, defines them in passing for an imagined non-informaticist listener, and connects them to terms from earlier modules.
Speaks about clinicians as if they were obstacles. Would lose the room in five seconds.
Acknowledges clinician concerns but treats them as problems to manage.
Speaks as a clinician to clinicians. Concerns are taken at face value.
Speaks as a clinician to clinicians AND surfaces concerns the skeptic had not yet voiced.
